title: Marvel's 'Wonder Man' Creators Joke About Winning an 'Auteur' Award
summary: Have you ever thought about who makes your favorite superhero shows? Destin Daniel Cretton and Andrew Guest are the co-creators of 'Wonder Man,' a Marvel series on Disney+. At a fancy awards ceremony called IndieWire Honors, they won the Auteur Award. But they started their speech with a joke! Cretton said, 'I'm pretty sure they never imagined the Auteur Award going to a Marvel series.' An auteur (oh-TUR) is a filmmaker with a very personal, artistic style—like Stanley Kubrick. But Cretton and Guest proved that even a superhero show can be art. 'Wonder Man' is a buddy comedy about a struggling actor. It's more about auditions than saving the universe! The creators thanked Marvel for taking risks and letting them make something different. They also thanked critics for helping people find the show. The ceremony was on June 4 in Los Angeles. So next time you watch a Marvel show, remember: it might be made by artists who love movies just as much as you do!
why_it_matters: It shows that even big superhero shows can be artistic and unique, reminding you that your own creative ideas matter, even in a group project.
